episode_title: Modernizing Life Insurance Workflows Through Agentic AI with Lars Boeing

real_qa.q: Why do companies learning to build software with AI still face high costs instead of free solutions?
real_qa.r: Even if building with AI, companies end up buying tokens instead of paying license fees, paying for consumption and addition. They still have to manage, maintain, and staff the system. Maintenance is not free and must be part of cost calculations. Additionally, SaaS providers offer best-in-class processes built into software from dozens or hundreds of clients, plus updated regulations and ongoing improvements that internal builders must replicate themselves.
real_qa.requete: AI software build costs tokens maintenance

real_qa.q: What is day two AI debt and why does it matter for agentic systems?
real_qa.r: Day two AI debt refers to ongoing maintenance problems that must be accounted for when deploying AI systems, including model deprecation and data line drift. These are essential considerations when engineering agentic systems, as they add significant complexity beyond the initial build phase.
real_qa.requete: day two AI debt model deprecation data drift

real_qa.q: How can agentic AI improve claims processing containment rates in life insurance?
real_qa.r: A life insurer working with Capgemini increased their claim status self-service rate from 45% containment with legacy IVR systems to 80% with agentic chatbot solutions, while simultaneously increasing customer satisfaction from 46% to 70%. The AI systems handle FNRL intake and claim status inquiries, failing gracefully by calling for human help when encountering situations above thresholds or never seen before.
real_qa.requete: life insurance claims AI self-service rate 80 percent

real_qa.q: What percentage of life insurer assets are held by policyholders aged 65 or older?
real_qa.r: Over 40% of all assets held by life insurers are bound to policyholders that are 65 or older, representing an immense amount of money prone to move out of the AUM pool if not addressed properly. Approximately two-thirds of this wealth transfer goes to beneficiaries aged 50 or older.
real_qa.requete: life insurance assets policyholders 65 years old wealth transfer

real_qa.q: How should claims adjusters' roles evolve with agentic AI implementation?
real_qa.r: One Capgemini client described the transformation as moving adjusters from firefighters to concierges. Technology takes burdensome reactive tasks off their plate—handling status calls, managing inquiries—and puts humans in a supervisory loop where they focus on thinking and decision-making rather than data entry or routine information lookups.
real_qa.requete: claims adjusters firefighters to concierge AI automation

guest.bio_context: Lars Boeing has spent more than 20 years in consulting and industry roles. He currently leads Capgemini Invent's global Future of Claims offering, helping insurers determine where agentic AI belongs in their business. His philosophy centers on augmenting people rather than replacing them, and optimizing processes before applying automation.

real_quote: We are augmenting humans. We are not replacing humans, right? We're making humans more efficient by providing them better tools.
